attempted_claim: Let M be an o-minimal expansion of a real closed field and let d>=3. What is the smallest exponent t(d) such that every formula phi(x;y) with |x|=d admits a distal cell decomposition T with |T(B)|=O_phi(|B|^t(d)) for all finite nonempty B? In particular, is the current general upper bound t(d)<=2d-2 tight — does some phi require exponent 2d-2 — or does every such phi admit exponent <=2d-3, possibly down to the dual VC-density lower bound d?
decisive_failure: The lane established only negative evidence: reconstruction of the published 2d-2 induction, the density-versus-pure-exponent distinction blocking the 2d-3 route, the type-counting cap at exponent d blocking the tightness route, and bounded grid computations confirming Theta(n^d) growth for natural candidates. No upper-bound improvement, tightness witness, or emergent theorem was proved; the optimal exponent t(d) remains open.
